kank:study:1.title: New unenlagiid from the Chorrillo Formation (Late Cretaceous, Maastrichtian), SW Patagonia, Argentina (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: The genus Kank was discovered in the Chorrillo Formation in southwestern Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: The remains of Kank were uncovered from the Maastrichtian-aged Chorrillo Formation ('Monotreme site') located in southwestern Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype of Kank is a single vertebra designated as specimen MPM-PV-23106-A.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is MPM-PV-23106-A, and consists of a single vertebra.

facts.statement: Three toe bones and five teeth were found alongside the holotype vertebra.
facts.quote: Three pedal phalanges and five teeth were found in the same spot as the holotype.

facts.statement: The genus name Kank honors the "elder Rhea" from Aonikenk mythology, who created the Southern Cross constellation.
facts.quote: The genus name "Kank" references the "elder Rhea" who, in Aonikenk mythology, created the constellation Choiols (the Southern Cross).

facts.statement: The species name australis means "from the south" in Latin, referring to the discovery location.
facts.quote: The specific name "australis" is a Latin word meaning "from the south", referencing the geographic region of the species' discovery.

facts.statement: Kank lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: Age: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: Kank lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kank lived in a wetland environment containing both terrestrial and freshwater areas, evidenced by associated fish fossils.
facts.quote: The Chorrillo Formation from which Kank is known represents a predominantly wetland environment, which included both terrestrial and freshwater conditions, and its fossils have been found in association with numerous fish remains.

facts.statement: The genus Kank contains only one species, Kank australis, known from fragmentary fossils.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Kank australis, known from fragmentary remains.

facts.statement: Kank was a medium-sized unenlagiid dinosaur with bones comparable in size to Neuquenraptor.
facts.quote: Kank is a medium-sized unenlagiid, with bones similar in size to Neuquenraptor.

facts.statement: The estimated mass of the similar dinosaur Neuquenraptor is 27 kg.
facts.quote: The mass of the latter has been estimated at 27 kg.

facts.statement: Kank possessed small, apically curved teeth that lacked serrations.
facts.quote: The teeth of Kank are small, curved apically, and lack serrations.

facts.statement: The upper jaw teeth of Kank were straight and lacked lingual curvature.
facts.quote: The maxillary teeth are straight and do not have lingual curvature.

facts.statement: Kank's teeth featured apicobasally oriented flutes around lateral grooves but no serrated ridges.
facts.quote: They also bear apicobasally oriented flutes surrounding lateral grooves and have no serrated carinae.

facts.statement: The lower jaw teeth of Kank had mesial ridges restricted to the top third of the crown, similar to Austroraptor.
facts.quote: Its dentary teeth have their mesial carinae restricted to the apical third of the crown as seen in Austroraptor.

facts.statement: Like Buitreraptor, the upper jaw teeth of Kank were compressed from side to side in cross-section.
facts.quote: Similar to Buitreraptor, its maxillary teeth are labiolingually compressed when seen in cross-section.

facts.statement: Kank is classified as a member of the unenlagiid theropod group.
facts.quote: Notes: A unenlagiid theropod.

facts.statement: The parent group of Kank is the family Unenlagiidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Unenlagiidae

facts.statement: Kank belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Kank was described by Motta and colleagues.
facts.quote: Authors: Motta et al.

facts.statement: The description of Kank was authored by Matías J. Motta, Alexis M. Aranciaga Rolando, and eleven other researchers.
facts.quote: Authors: Matías J. Motta, Alexis M. Aranciaga Rolando, Sebastián Rozadilla, Federico L. Agnolín, Federico Brissón Egli, Gerardo P. Álvarez Herrera, Nicolás R. Chimento, Gastón Lo Coco, Takanobu Tsuihiji, Makoto Manabe, Diego Pol, Fernando E. Novas

facts.statement: The type locality for Kank is the Chorrillo Formation.
facts.quote: Type locality: Chorrillo Formation

facts.statement: Kank was found in Argentina.
facts.quote: Country: Argentina

facts.statement: Kank is currently considered a valid taxon.
facts.quote: Status: Valid

facts.statement: Kank represents a new genus and new species.
facts.quote: Novelty: Gen. et sp. nov

facts.statement: Kank is the first unenlagiid dinosaur recorded from the Chorrillo Formation.
facts.quote: The discovery of Kank makes it the first member of the family Unenlagiidae that has been recorded from the Chorrillo Formation

facts.statement: Additional remains potentially belonging to Kank include a dorsal vertebra, a toe claw, and isolated teeth.
facts.quote: Several additional remains from this formation may belong to Kank, including a dorsal vertebral centrum originally identified as belonging to a megaraptoran, a pedal ungual (toe claw), and isolated teeth.

rejected.statement: Kank is an extinct genus of unenlagiid paravian dinosaur.
rejected.quote: Kank is an extinct genus of unenlagiid paravian dinosaur
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Kank is an extinct genus of unenlagiid paravian'
